targetText: The universality or absoluteness of contradiction has a twofold meaning. One is that contradiction exists in the process of development of all things, and the other is that in the process of development of each thing a movement of opposites exists from beginning to end.
explanation: Tension and opposing forces exist in everything, from science to human relationships, from the moment something begins until it ends. Real-life example: In physical fitness, building muscle requires breaking down muscle fibers through stress so they grow back stronger. Tension exists from start to finish.

targetText: There is nothing that does not contain contradiction; without contradiction nothing would exist.
explanation: Nothing in the universe is completely static or without internal tension. Real-life example: An ecosystem exists only because predators and prey, plants and soil nutrients continuously interact and balance against each other.

targetText: Opposition and struggle between ideas of different kinds constantly occur within the Party; this is a reflection within the Party of contradictions between classes and between the new and the old in society.
explanation: Disagreements inside a team or political group are not random mistakes; they reflect real competing pressures from the broader world. Real-life example: In a community group, debates between members who want immediate spending versus long-term saving reflect real economic pressures facing different households.
